field.label: Enable
field.help: Enable the TFTP proxy. Requires a firewall port-forward rule redirecting UDP/69 to the listen address and port configured below.

field.label: Listen Address
field.help: The IPv4 address on which tftp-proxy listens via inetd(8). Use 127.0.0.1 when redirecting via a pf(4) rdr rule.

field.label: Listen Port
field.help: The UDP port on which tftp-proxy listens (default 6969). Create a NAT port-forward rule redirecting incoming UDP/69 to this port.

field.label: Verbose Logging
field.help: Pass -v to tftp-proxy for verbose connection logging to syslog.

field.label: Proxy Timeout
field.help: Seconds tftp-proxy keeps its temporary pf(4) rule (and holds a process open) after relaying a request, before assuming the transfer is under way and cleaning up (tftp-proxy's -w flag, default 2). Each request occupies tftp-proxy for at least this long, so a busy client that retries aggressively (e.g. searching many candidate config filenames) can queue up faster than tftp-proxy can drain if this is set higher than your network's actual round-trip time requires. Lower it toward your real server round-trip time to raise the sustainable request rate before that backlog causes lookups to start failing.
